nodes.name: adp-usb-eth
nodes.description:
USB 3.0 gigabit dongle. `upstream.attached_to` is what joins it to the
laptop - there is deliberately no cable between the two (NV-X005).

nodes.name: laptop
nodes.description:
Ultrabook without a built-in Ethernet port. It reaches the wired network
through the USB dongle declared in hosts/adp-usb-eth.yaml, so it owns no
cabled interface of its own.

nodes.name: phone
nodes.description:
Wireless-only client. It reaches the network through its association to
ap-home, which is declared as a `medium: wireless` cable - the association
is the link.

interfaces.name: en0
interfaces.description: Associated to the home SSID on 5 GHz

nodes.name: rtr-home
nodes.description:
Home edge router. Terminates the ISP hand-off on wan0 and is the default
gateway for the single home VLAN (10).

nodes.name: sw-home
nodes.description: Eight-port desktop switch in the hallway cabinet

interfaces.name: Vlan10
interfaces.description: In-band management address of the switch

interfaces.name: port4
interfaces.description: Patch to the desk, used by the laptop dongle

interfaces.name: port5
interfaces.description: PoE injector for ap-home; trunks the guest VLAN up to it

nodes.name: ap-home
nodes.description:
Ceiling access point in the hallway, powered over the uplink. It is a
switch: the radio is a bridge port like any other, and the two SSIDs are
what it bridges the air into.

interfaces.name: br0
interfaces.description: Bridges the radio onto the wired uplink

interfaces.name: Vlan10
interfaces.description: In-band management address of the access point
